newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Stg/mark to use 2.8820 as base for rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Stg/mark to use 2.8820 as base for rally.

text.p: Sterling will use $1.6550 and 2.8820 marks as bases from which to claw back ground it lost Tuesday, analysts said.

If these levels turn out to be strong enough props, the pound is expected to resume its assault on the five-year high of 2.91 marks it set yesterday, and make a renewed bid to take out the five-month high of $1.6725 it reached just over a week ago.

"The pullbacks in cable and sterling/mark have seen both rates test key corrective levels," said Ian Stannard, technical analyst at Chase Investment Bank. "If these supports prove effective, we will maintain the upward trend."
Sterling was at 2.8953/63 at 0805 GMT from 2.8875/85 late Tuesday in Europe. Cable was at $1.6585/95 from $1.6575/80 yesterday.
On its way up, the pound tested 2.8820 marks on June 24 and 26 before finally bursting through it to set new five-year highs. This level is therefore expected to offer good support.
A break below this level will, however, signal a deeper correction to 2.8570 marks. Sterling used this area as a base on which to consolidate the previous leg of its rally.
"Use 2.88 (marks) as triggers for 2.86/2.8570," said Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank.
"We do not really think that a major top is in place but a significant correction is still working through."
Celaya said a break above 2.90 would pave the way for a move back to 2.9100/20 for sterling/mark, and eventually to 2.93/95.
Cable's key support of $1.6550 marks the top end of its trading range from early April until the breakout in mid June.
"Holding above here is very important and if we do, it will allow a rest of $1.6725," said Stannard at Chase.
Any rebound in cable will encounter initial resistance at $1.6600, the level which it offered it solid support between June 24 and 27 before finally giving way yesterday.
